newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 59.23 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 59.23 PCT.

text.p: The average rate for Romania's central bank's one-week funds rose sharply to 59.23 percent at this week's refinancing auction from 53 percent in a previous session, central bank data showed on Friday.

The central bank's offer of 2.15 trillion lei, down from a previous 2.315 trillion, was heavily undersubscribed with two banks entering bids totaling 1.363 trillion at prices ranging from 57 to 60 percent.
The central bank has recently started to tighten its monetary policies in a move to calm down a surge of inflation and in line with International Monetary Fund recommendations.

At Thursday's auction the bank raised the minimum permitted rate for one-week funds by four percentage points to 57 percent, after jacking up the discount rate to 50 percent from 35 percent earlier this week.
Year-on-year inflation rose to 47.4 percent last November from October's 45.1 percent, exceeding the 20 percent target agreed with the IMF for 1996.
Inflation is seen quickening after Romania's new centrist government doubled fuel prices starting January to bring them to world levels and meet the Fund's recommendations.
The IMF suspended a three-year standby credit of $460 million after criticising the lax policies of the leftist government ousted in last November's general election.
Short-term inter-bank money market prices, now trading at around 56 percent, are expected to rise in line with the tighter monetary policy.
An IMF mission is expected to arrive in Bucharest this month to discuss a new loan accord with the new cabinet. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
